steps: The main temperature scales are the Celsius scale, the Fahrenheit scale and the Kelvin scale.
items.finalAnswer: Celsius, Fahrenheit and Kelvin are the main scales used to measure temperature.

steps: The sensitivity of a thermometer is its ability to detect small changes in temperature.
A thermometer is more sensitive when a small change in temperature produces a large change in its thermometric property.
items.finalAnswer: Sensitivity is the ability of a thermometer to detect small changes in temperature.

steps: The linearity of a thermometer is the property by which equal changes in temperature produce equal changes in its thermometric property.
items.finalAnswer: Linearity means equal temperature changes produce equal changes in the thermometer’s thermometric property.

steps: A thermometer should be read with the eye level with the top of the liquid column.
This avoids parallax error and makes the scale reading accurate.
items.finalAnswer: Read the thermometer at eye level with the top of the liquid column to avoid parallax error.

steps: The temperature difference between two bodies determines the direction of heat flow.
Heat flows from the body at higher temperature to the body at lower temperature.
items.finalAnswer: Heat flows from a higher-temperature body to a lower-temperature body.

steps: Heat is energy transferred from one body to another because of a temperature difference.
Internal energy is the total kinetic and potential energy of the molecules of a body.
Heat is energy in transit, whereas internal energy is the energy possessed by a body.
items.finalAnswer: Heat is energy transferred due to a temperature difference; internal energy is the total kinetic and potential energy of a body’s molecules.

steps: Cold does not travel from the surface to your hand.
Energy flows from your warmer hand to the colder surface.
items.finalAnswer: Energy travels from your hand to the cold surface; cold does not travel.

steps: No. Touching your own forehead does not reliably tell you whether you have a fever.
The sensation of warmth depends on the temperature difference between your hand and forehead, so a thermometer is needed to measure your temperature accurately.
items.finalAnswer: No. Touch alone cannot reliably detect a fever; use a thermometer to measure temperature.
